fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Each Workflow
fields.features_subheading: Each workflow Emergent builds is an app with its own database, and every run leaves a record you can open.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt, one working app

Emergent builds the workflow and the database behind it from a plain-English prompt. When a rule changes, such as a new due date or a second approver, ask for it in a new prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Connected to the tools you already use

The app connects to any tool with an API, such as QuickBooks, HubSpot, Stripe, or Slack. Data syncs in and out, and nobody retypes a client's details from one screen into another.
fields.feature_3:
Alerts for the step that stalls

Pick how long a step can wait and who is told when it waits longer. Reminders go out by email or as a Slack message, and the owner hears once a step runs past the wait you set.
fields.feature_4:
Receipts and invoices read into fields

The app reads receipts, invoices, and filled-in forms into structured fields with AI. Any field the AI is unsure of lands in a review queue, and a person confirms it first.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap on a busy month

Workflows Emergent builds carry no task cap. A spring rush of 400 service requests runs through the same rules as a slow week, and the workflow keeps running as volume climbs.
fields.feature_6:
The code behind your workflows, in GitHub

Export the full code of each workflow to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer you hire later can read every rule and trigger, and change them like any other code.

fields.tab_content_1:
A request nobody answers by 11:40 goes to the owner

A web request for a furnace repair reaches Drumhallow Heating and Air at 9:40 a.m. from zip code 30318. The app assigns it to Hollis Harbottle, the tech who covers that zip, and messages him in Slack. By 11:40 a.m. nobody has marked it contacted, and the owner, Gideon Tregarthen, gets a Slack alert.
fields.tab_content_2:
Invoice #2216 for $1,480 gets a second reminder

Each morning, the app reads Thimbleby Lawn and Garden's open invoices from QuickBooks. Invoice #2216 to Pettifer Court HOA for $1,480 is 14 days past due, and the HOA gets its second reminder email. The first went out at 7 days. At 21 days past due, the invoice becomes a call task for the owner, Wilhelmina Chaudry.
fields.tab_content_3:
Corisande gets a kickoff task when Ridley Park accepts

Ridley Park Orthodontics accepts a $9,600 proposal from Caddick Design Studio for a new website. The app emails the practice an intake questionnaire and gives the project lead, Corisande Velling, a kickoff task. If the questionnaire is still blank after 3 days, the practice gets a reminder email.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bram gets a 120 kg reorder to approve at 48 kg

Kestlemoor Coffee Roasters logs each roast in the app, and every batch draws down its green coffee. After Tuesday's roasts, the Colombian lot sits at 48 kg against a 60 kg reorder point. The app drafts a 120 kg reorder and sends it to the owner, Bram Okonjo-Wilde, to approve in the app.

fields.howto_title: How to Automate Small Business Workflows
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to pick the first job worth handing off, then build workflow automation for small business around it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every task that repeats
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the trigger and the rule
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name one person for each exception
fields.howto_step_1_des: Keep a list for one week of every task someone on your team does more than once, such as sending a quote or chasing a payment. Next to each one, write who does it and about how many minutes it takes each time.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Multiply each task's minutes by how often it happens in a month, and start with the biggest total. A 10-minute task done 60 times a month costs 10 hours, more than a 2-hour report you write once.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the workflow in one sentence that names what starts it and what happens next. "When an invoice is 7 days past due, email the client" is a workflow. "Stay on top of invoices" is a wish, and no app can run it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who hears about it when the rule cannot settle a case, such as a request nobody answers. Give each exception one named person and a wait time, and send the alert to that person instead of a shared inbox.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the sentence from step 3 and the names from step 4 into a prompt. Emergent builds the workflow and its database from that description, and a new rule later arrives the same way, by describing the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Link the apps the workflow reads from or writes to, such as your accounting system for invoices or Slack for alerts. Map each field once, and check that a client's name in the app matches the name on the invoice.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run it on last week's work
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the workflow goes live, replay last week's real requests and invoices through it. Check that every alert reached the right person at the right time, then switch it on for new work coming in.

faq_plan.q: What is workflow automation for small business?
faq_plan.a: Workflow automation for small business is software that runs a repeating job on a rule: when something happens, the app does the next step without anyone starting it. A person on the team hears about a case only when it needs a decision.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up workflow automation for small business?
faq_plan.a: Pick one job that repeats every week, and write its rule as one sentence with a trigger and an action. Describe that rule to Emergent's AI automation builder, which turns it into a working app that keeps its own records. Then run a week of past cases through it before new work arrives.

faq_plan.q: Can small business automation work without a developer on staff?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A workflow can be written as plain sentences about the trigger and the action that follows, and the person who runs the process today is the best one to write them. Emergent builds the app from a prompt in plain English, with no code to write.

faq_plan.q: Which jobs in a small business suit workflow automation best?
faq_plan.a: Jobs that start from a date or a new record suit it best. A brokerage that sends each showing request to the listing agent is running real estate workflow automation in its simplest form. A cleaning company emails a review request two days after each job. A print shop moves an order to production once the customer approves the proof.

faq_plan.q: How do I know a small business process is ready for workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: It is ready when the same steps happen in the same order every time, and you can say what starts it. If two people on your team would handle the same case differently, agree on one rule and write it down before anything gets built.

faq_plan.q: Can a small business try workflow automation for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and its free tier covers building and publishing. Build the one workflow from your list that costs the most hours, run it on real cases for a few weeks, and judge it by the hours it gives back.

faq_plan.q: How does a small law or accounting business use workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: A small firm automates the intake and deadline side of the work and keeps the advice with people. New client intake and a reminder before each filing date are good first workflows, and legal workflow automation covers that pattern in detail. The attorney or accountant who signs off still makes every judgment call.

faq_plan.q: What should stay manual in workflow automation for a small business?
faq_plan.a: Keep the steps that need judgment or a relationship, such as pricing a custom job or answering an upset customer. Let the workflow gather the facts and route the case, then have one named person make the call.

faq_plan.q: Who owns the customer data when a small business uses workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Your business should own it, and the tool you build with decides whether you do. In apps Emergent builds, the data lives in a database you own. Before you commit to any tool, ask where its records sit and how you get a full copy out.

faq_plan.q: Can a tutoring business or small school use workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A tutoring business can send each new student's intake form to the right tutor and email parents a reminder the day before each session. Education workflow automation covers the school side, with jobs such as enrollment forms and attendance follow-up.
